decisive_items: She received intramuscular methotrexate (50 mg/m2) on day 1
Shortly thereafter, she noted pain and swelling in both knees
Both knees were diffusely swollen and tender to palpation
response.rationale: The bilateral knee inflammation occurred shortly after methotrexate exposure for ectopic pregnancy, with elevated inflammatory markers and joint effusions but no fever or evident infection, best fitting a methotrexate-induced rheumatologic inflammatory reaction.

rejected.why: Ectopic pregnancy explains the initial presentation but not the new bilateral knee arthritis after methotrexate treatment.
Septic arthritis is less likely because the patient is afebrile, appears well, has bilateral rather than monoarticular involvement, and there is no synovial fluid/culture evidence of infection.
Rheumatoid arthritis is a chronic autoimmune polyarthritis and does not explain the acute post-methotrexate temporal pattern.
Reactive arthritis is possible but no urethritis/enteritis precipitating infection is described; the dominant temporal clue is methotrexate exposure.
